proposals.title: Zoom Shorts have no breakout reference yet
proposals.change: Keep zoom-inside Shorts at most 2 in 5 until one of ours proves the shape; their only Short references are Branch Education's (504K-1.0M views on 2.78M subscribers, 0.2-0.4x), which check-plan rejects as demand. Tonight's zoom topics now cite Silicon Up Close's 'What Happens Inside an AI Chip When You Ask a Question' (1.02M on 12.7K, 80.6x) and PROCESS BHARAT's chipmaking video (2.2M on 234K, 9.4x).
proposals.expectedEffect: plans built on zoom topics pass check-plan; the mix leans on invention Shorts, whose references are real breakouts
proposals.risk: zoom Shorts may still work for us; our own numbers decide

proposals.title: Rank the topic feed by traction, not only total views (owner note, 19 Nov)
proposals.change: In generator/topics.py score_parts, add a 'traction' part from demand.viewsPerDay and demand.ageDays (both now written by research on new topics): a reference under 30 days old adds up to +1.0 on a log scale of views per day (10K/day = +0.3, 100K/day = +0.7, 300K+/day = +1.0); a reference over 90 days old adds nothing. Topics without the fields score as today. Research keeps writing viewsPerDay/ageDays from the niche scan.
evidence: niche-data scan 18 Nov: last-14-day Shorts by subject vs their channel's median: invention 2.54x, trains 2.40x, phones 1.84x, planes 1.77x, chips 1.68x, AI 1.12x, rocket/space 0.90x
Owner note cmwn0yhck0001jj0928f6obym: 'choose topics which are gaining traction'
proposals.expectedEffect: The planner takes topics whose reference is rising this month (e.g. maglev, 234K views/day) ahead of evergreen ones with a big but old reference.
proposals.risk: Over-weights one fast channel's spike; capped at +1.0 so demand and breakout still dominate.
proposals.note: generator/topics.py traction(): views a day of a reference under 30 days, faded to 0 by 90 days, +0 to +1.0
